expected_generation.description: Exact served_generation acquired from one complete, stable fishhat.dns.observe traversal under this custodian and approved executor. Revalidate the complete identity and every before-RRset immediately before publication under native exclusion. An incomplete, unknown, stale or mixed-generation traversal cannot authorize a change.

description: Each change adds, deletes or replaces one RRset identity. Before and after cannot both be null, and non-null replacements retain the same name, class and type. RDATA member order is insignificant: a reorder-only before/after pair is a no-op and rejects. TTL policy and ordered content inside each member remain significant. expected_generation.owner equals custodian; its binding is DNS role and its scope equals scope. Observe, publish and reconcile use the same DNSGeneration type; no integer-to-digest conversion is permitted. A native provider unable to establish exact revision and before-state prerequisites must refuse publication. Successful reconciliation preserves the original attempt and generation namespace; it cannot adopt a replacement service.

DNSGeneration.description: One receiver-maintained authoritative DNS revision namespace. owner is the receiving custodian including epoch; binding is its exact independently approved DNS executor and scope; native_incarnation identifies the protected authoritative service incarnation; generation is a durable monotonic counter within that exact namespace. It is not an SOA serial, artifact digest, request digest or owner resource generation. The counter changes whenever authoritative scoped RRset state changes, including external edits; a successful nonempty publication returns a strictly newer value. A restore, replacement, lost counter continuity or untrackable external changes invalidates prior observations: establish a fresh native incarnation or return unknown, never reuse a counter as current authority. Identical RRsets after an intervening change do not restore an old revision. The native owner must establish and recheck this identity under atomic prerequisites or equivalent exclusion; these fields do not themselves prove native enforcement.
